answers.core:
This must be core because:
- Export Presets are part of the engine’s build pipeline, not accessible from add-ons.
- Conditional compilation (`#if`) in _C#_ requires compiler flags, which cannot be injected by add-ons.
answers.workaround:
No.

- In _C#_, runtime checks (`if (OS.HasFeature("steamworks"))`) cannot replace compile-time directives. Unused code still gets compiled, and missing external libraries (like _Steamworks.NET_) may cause runtime errors.
- Using separate .pck files for different exports can partially separate resources, but it is tedious and does not stop _C#_ scripts from being compiled for all targets.
- The only practical workaround I have found (but not tested) is to always perform exports from the command line (using custom build scripts or CI pipelines that pass different compiler flags or use different project configurations per build). This approach is cumbersome, fragile, and does not integrate with the Editor’s Export Presets.

title: Allow defining custom environment variables in Export Presets (C#)
